finishes.mechanism_summary:
Two Ronchi rulings (50%-duty gratings antialiased to a fixed ~1.15px edge, so at a 2.6-3.0px pitch they are near-triangular — the unresolved-ruling regime a real instrument runs in) are laid across each other about a seeded bisector. The rendered field is the transmitted PRODUCT g1*g2, whose local average beats at d = pitch/(2 sin(cross/2)).

The parameterisation is inverted from the obvious one: `fringe` (the beat d, in pixels) is the knob and the crossing angle is SOLVED from it, `half = arcsin(pitch/(2*fringe))`. That is deliberate — the beat is the dominant structure and the SCALE gate is a cliff on its size, so the thing the gate measures has to be the thing the author sets.

The deflectometry is real. A specimen — a seeded analytic saddle (panel form) plus sparse local defects from `nz*|nz|` over two incommensurate noise lattices — is differentiated ONCE along the ruling normal (the only slope component that deflects a ray) and injected into G1's coordinate as a lateral displacement of its self-image at the plane of G2, scaled so `orders` reads directly in fringe orders at 3 sigma. Because deflection enters as a PHASE SHIFT and never as brightness, the fringes become contours of constant surface SLOPE: they sweep with panel curvature and fork, crowd and dislocate around a defect. The specimen itself is invisible, which is the technique, and it also means the macro field contributes almost no coarse energy (measured coarse 0.002 at 2048, 0.015 at 1024).

The deflection is soft-saturated rather than clipped: `defl = dW/(1 + |dW|*0.5/swing)`. This bounds the phase GRADIENT as well as the value, with the compression strongest exactly where the slope is steepest. With a hard clip the canvas corners aliased into visible hash, because the saddle's gradient grows linearly outward and the carrier sits near Nyquist.

One box of two ruling periods nulls the carrier and every harmonic (sinc(2n)=0) and leaves the beat at ~0.73; the residual prod-avg IS the carrier, reused free at `bar_mix` strength so the barely-resolved ruling still grains the fringe. Paint modulates the painter's colour multiplicatively, adds a transmitted-light term gated on the paint's own headroom (a deflectogram is formed in transmission, so it survives on a near-black livery), and applies a ±0.17 rad chromatic swing for the ruled edge's dispersion — this technique images monochrome, so the base colour survives on red, blue, gold and near-black.

THE DRAFT WAS NOT CORRECT. It fails the SCALE gate outright, and its look does not do what its own docstring claims. Both were found by measurement, not reading. What I changed and why:

FATAL — SCALE. The draft's dominant structure is an 18.1px beat. Run through the law's own `scale_axis`, that scores 0.694 at 2048 and **0.114 at 1024, against a 0.20 floor, with coarse 0.671**. Both `scripts/spb_finish_law.py` and `scripts/spb_variant_search.py` default to RES=1024, and `scale_axis` takes the FFT ring between radii 64 and 256 — those bounds are FIXED constants (2048/32 and 2048/8), while a p-pixel feature sits at radius n/p. So a 1024 render judges an absolute p as if it were 2p: in-band is 4-16px at 1024 and 8-32px at 2048, and only the intersection 8-16px passes both. The draft's self-audit reports "measured at 2048" and never checked the resolution the gate actually runs at. I re-parameterised so the beat is a direct knob spanning 10.5-14.0px (FFT radius 73-98 at 1024, 146-195 at 2048) and confirmed the 16px cliff empirically: a 16.1px beat collapses to SCALE 0.074 / coarse 0.699 at 1024.

LOOK — the mechanism was invisible. At the draft's `lever`, the fringes render as straight corduroy at 1:1: total deviation under one fringe order, so "a dent closes a fringe loop" never happens. Raising deflection on the draft's geometry does not fix it — with a 2.5px pitch the carrier is already at 80% of Nyquist, and at ~7 orders the bottom-right quarter of the 2048 canvas broke into aliased hash (confetti). Fixed three ways: `orders` now reads in fringe orders and spans 2.0-5.0; the specimen moved to a long scale (197/119px) so the bend happens over enough distance; and the hard clip became a soft saturation that bounds the gradient. The corner blowout is gone and the fringes now visibly sweep, fork and pinch around defects.

LOOK — lattice seams. `K.mid` bilinearly upsamples a coarse lattice (at 340px on a 2048 canvas that is a 6x6 grid), so its GRADIENT is discontinuous at every cell line and the directional difference printed straight seams across the fringes. Fixed with an analytic seeded saddle for the panel form plus two incommensurate lattices and one K.box(18). I tried removing the box in favour of a wider central difference: it brought the seams back as horizontal smears and moved coarse 0.030 -> 0.087, so the box stays.

WRONG COMMENT. The draft's `K.box(prod, round(pitch*0.5))` evaluates to r=2 (kernel 5) for EVERY pitch in its space, so its "a box of width p attenuates period p to sinc(1)=0" claim was false. Now `round(pitch-0.5)`, i.e. kernel ~2*pitch, which nulls the carrier and all its harmonics at sinc(2n)=0.

UNEARNED GRAMMAR. The draft's spec docstring claimed reads "along the two axes the crossed rulings define" but every channel was a pointwise function of t; nothing was directional. Added a real anisotropic member: `flank`, a roll-pair difference of the same field taken along the beat normal (k1-k2 is exactly proportional to (sin ang, -cos ang)), which tilts roughness. It cost nothing on FOLLOW (0.956 worst).

DARK BASES. Added a transmitted-light term gated on the paint's own headroom — dead at base 0.03 went 0.762 -> 0.479.

Also: `lever` (px) -> `orders` (fringe orders), `cross` -> `fringe` (px), K.norm -> a 3-sigma standardisation (min/max let one extreme squash the fringe), hue swing 0.26 -> 0.34.

(a) DOMINANT FEATURE SIZE — 12px, in 10-30 by construction. The dominant structure is the beat, and its spacing IS the `fringe` knob, so every point in the SPACE lands in 10.5-14.0px; measured spectral peak 10.5 / 12.3 / 14.1px at the corners, matching the knob to within 1%. The 2.6-3.0px carrier is sub-window on purpose (an unresolved ruling) and is capped by `bar_mix`; because it is near-triangular it carries weak harmonics, so it dilutes the SCALE denominator far less than a hard square would. The specimen is the only large-scale thing present and it carries NO brightness at all.

(b) EXACT EXPRESSION THE SPEC RECONSTRUCTS — `spec_` calls the same cached `_moire_deflect(shape, seed, _P(...))` the paint calls and gets the identical three arrays:
    fld   = clip(0.10 + 0.80*std3(box(g1*g2, round(pitch-0.5))) + bar_mix*1.8*(g1*g2 - box(g1*g2, round(pitch-0.5))), 0, 1)

with g = clip((0.25 - |u - floor(u) - 0.5|)*pitch/1.15 + 0.5, 0, 1). M is a 5-step ladder of t = 1 - fld, R a ramp in t tilted by flank, CC the complement of t; crest blends the second material into M and R. No independent spec field exists anywhere.

    20 points at RES=1024 (midpoint, all 12 single-knob extremes, 4 joint corners, 3 extra seeds) — ALL PASS.

(e) WHAT I AM STILL NOT SURE ABOUT —

If a shelf runner passes --res 2048, my SPACE is conservative (it would allow up to 32px); if it uses 1024, the draft's would have been fatal. Nothing in the SPACE fails either way, which is why I chose the intersection.

I grepped: existing moire work is concentric-ring rosettes (fractured_forge, arsenal_24k), a sum-of-two-sines `moire_beat` engine, and an anime Ben-Day halftone. None multiplies two square-wave rulings or injects a slope gradient as fringe phase. The shelf harness must still run the real gate.
 3. TRACK DISTANCE. At 4x downsample the fringes merge into a fine directional shimmer rather than staying legible as fringes. That is honest to a close-inspection image and the 8-32px window is where the metric looks, but if the shelf wants 50m readability, push `fringe` toward 14.0.

 5. `oy, ox = int(round(3.0*s1)), int(round(3.0*c1))` cannot both be zero (max(|s1|,|c1|) >= 0.707, so 3*0.707 rounds to 2). Same for the flank's `step >= 2`. If anyone tunes either constant below ~0.71 a zero-guard must come back.

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════ FL · SHEAROGRAPHY ══
def _shearo(shape, seed, P):
    """Laser shearing interferometry — two real optical stages, in order.

    1. OBJECTIVE SPECKLE. A rough surface under coherent light returns a random
       walk of phasors, so the complex amplitude A = ar + i*ai is a BAND-LIMITED
       GAUSSIAN field and the sensor records |A|^2 = ar*ar + ai*ai — negative
       exponential: a dark ground with hot grains. The band limit IS the imaging
       aperture, which is why the quadratures are blurred BEFORE squaring;
       blurring the intensity instead gives mush with none of the statistics.
       The two lattices are deliberately incommensurate (g and 0.77g): measured,
       a single lattice left a faint square grid at exactly `grain`.

    2. CORRELATION FRINGES. Shearography does not measure out-of-plane
       displacement w, it measures w(x+dx) - w(x), so `surf - roll(surf, 16)` IS
       the shearing element, not a stand-in. A disbond bulges under load and the
       sheared difference of a round bulge is the two-lobed BUTTERFLY with a null
       down its middle. Specimen tilt supplies the straight carrier every real
       head shows, so a defect reads as a LOCAL DISTORTION of a uniform field.

    That last point is what keeps SCALE honest: the disbonds are ~150px across
    yet carry ZERO coarse contrast — the fringe amplitude is uniform everywhere
    and the defect only bends phase. Measured on the law's own maths (RES 1024,
    8-32px-at-2048 annulus): paint band 0.788, coarse 0.201.
    """
    h, w = shape[:2]

    def build():
        # ---- 1. the coherent carrier ----------------------------------------
        g = float(P["grain"])
        rad = max(1, int(round(g * 0.30)))
        ar = K.box(K.mid((h, w), g, seed + 21, octaves=1) - np.float32(0.5), rad)
        ai = K.box(K.mid((h, w), g * 0.77, seed + 22, octaves=1) - np.float32(0.5), rad)
        np.multiply(ar, ar, out=ar)
        np.multiply(ai, ai, out=ai)
        ar += ai                              # |A|^2
        del ai
        # Normalising by 2*mean rather than by max keeps the exponential tail —
        # a handful of grains blow out, which is what speckle actually does.
        ar *= np.float32(1.0 / max(float(ar.mean()) * 2.0, 1e-6))
        spk = np.clip(ar, 0.0, 1.0, out=ar)

        # ---- 2. the specimen: a bonded skin with a scatter of disbonds -------
        # Folded coordinates, not a per-defect loop: one warped 210px lattice
        # gives an unbounded field of round C1 domes in ~10 array ops. The first
        # cut built this by box-blurring a coarse noise field and measured 0.31s
        # of a 3s budget for a diamond-faceted bulge; this is rounder and free.
        inv = np.float32(1.0 / 210.0)
        u = K.mid((h, w), 340.0, seed + 31, octaves=1) - np.float32(0.5)
        u *= np.float32(120.0)
        u += np.arange(h, dtype=np.float32)[:, None]
        u *= inv
        v = K.mid((h, w), 340.0, seed + 32, octaves=1) - np.float32(0.5)
        v *= np.float32(120.0)
        v += np.arange(w, dtype=np.float32)[None, :]
        v *= inv
        u -= np.floor(u)
        u -= np.float32(0.5)
        v -= np.floor(v)
        v -= np.float32(0.5)
        np.multiply(u, u, out=u)
        np.multiply(v, v, out=v)
        u += v
        u *= np.float32(1.0 / (0.36 * 0.36))
        np.clip(u, 0.0, 1.0, out=u)
        u -= np.float32(1.0)
        np.multiply(u, u, out=u)              # C1 dome, peak 1.0 at the site
        v = K.mid((h, w), 470.0, seed + 33, octaves=2) - np.float32(P["bond"])
        v *= np.float32(4.0)
        np.clip(v, 0.0, 1.0, out=v)
        u *= v                                # only some sites have let go
        del v

        d = u - np.roll(u, 16, axis=1)        # <- the shearing element
        del u

        # `orders` is normalised against the measured peak of d, so it means what
        # it says (fringe orders at the worst defect) whatever the geometry does,
        # and the local fringe period near a defect cannot alias: the steepest
        # phase gradient at orders=8 is 0.74 rad/px -> a 8.4px local period.
        gain = np.float32(float(P["orders"]) * 6.2832
                          / max(float(d.max()), -float(d.min()), 1e-5))
        ang = 0.22 + 0.62 * (((int(seed) * 2654435761) % 997) / 997.0)
        kk = 6.2832 / float(P["pitch"])
        d *= gain
        d += np.arange(h, dtype=np.float32)[:, None] * np.float32(kk * np.sin(ang))
        d += np.arange(w, dtype=np.float32)[None, :] * np.float32(kk * np.cos(ang))
        np.cos(d, out=d)
        d *= np.float32(-0.46)
        d += np.float32(0.54)                 # 0.08 + 0.92 * (0.5 - 0.5cos ph)

        # Fringe and speckle keep their OWN pedestals. Measured: with one shared
        # pedestal the speckle (sd/mean ~1) buried the fringes and the whole
        # finish read as flat cloth at 3:1.
        sl = np.float32(P["spkl"])
        spk *= (np.float32(1.0) - sl)
        spk += sl
        d *= spk
        return np.clip(d, 0, 1, out=d)

    return K.cache(("flshear", h, w, int(seed), _k(P)), build)


def paint_fl_shearography(paint, shape, mask, seed, pm, bb):
    """The monitor image of a shearography head: fringes carried on laser speckle."""
    P = _P("fl_shearography")
    src = K.incoming(paint, shape)
    vis = _shearo(shape, seed, P)
    drive = np.float32(float(P["drive"]) * (0.55 + 0.45 * float(pm)))
    # Peak-normalised so `drive` buys CONTRAST, never exposure: measured, the raw
    # 0.46 + drive*vis blew 47% of a white base past 0.94 at drive 1.55; this
    # holds it to 15% and leaves band_abs higher (0.135 vs 0.051) either way.
    bn = np.float32(1.18 / (0.46 + float(drive)))
    # Monochromatic illumination: the ground is the painter's own colour returned
    # at ONE wavelength. hue_rotate runs on the MEAN colour — a 1x1x3 array —
    # not the canvas, which is ~15 full-canvas ops saved for the same result on a
    # flat base. The exposure normalisation is the head gaining up, and it has to
    # be a real normalisation: a 0.25 floor there left a near-black base 89% dead.
    c = src.mean(axis=(0, 1))
    c = np.clip(c + (c - float(c.mean())) * 1.8, 0.02, 1.0)
    c = c / max(float(c.max()), 0.02)
    lasr = np.clip(K.hue_rotate(c.reshape(1, 1, 3), 0.42), 0, 1).reshape(3)
    hot = np.clip((vis - np.float32(0.62)) * np.float32(2.9), 0, 1)
    hot *= hot                                # grains that blew out the sensor
    hot *= np.float32(0.40) * drive * bn
    emit = vis * vis                          # returned intensity, ADDITIVE: the
    emit *= np.float32(0.34) * drive * bn     # sensor image is emitted light, and
    emit += hot                               # a multiplicative-only build left a
    body = vis * drive                        # near-black base 89% dead (now 69%).
    body += np.float32(0.46)
    body *= bn
    out = src * body[:, :, None]
    for ch in range(3):                       # 3 channel adds, not one HxWx3 temp
        out[:, :, ch] += float(lasr[ch]) * emit
    return K.finish(out, src, mask)


def spec_fl_shearography(shape, seed, sm, base_m, base_r):
    """GRAMMAR: speckle-modulated smooth ramp — nothing quantised anywhere.

    The correlation image is a continuous field, so the material is a continuous
    ramp off it. `mod` is the paint's own luminance envelope rebuilt term for
    term — same pedestal, same drive, same quadratic emission, same hot term —
    so FOLLOW is true by construction rather than by argument. The peak
    normaliser `bn` cancels exactly under K.norm (it multiplies every term),
    which is why it is absent here. Measured amp_corr 0.998.

    Background (M,R,CC) = 15 / 190 / 90 — a matte dielectric composite skin,
    which is WHY the part speckles at all: a mirror returns no objective speckle.
    Up the ramp the hot grains are facets that caught the beam square, so they go
    slightly metallic, tighter and glossier together. Measured medians on the
    law's own 0.5-grey base: 21.5 / 181.9 / 89.2, dominant cell (0,4,2) at 59%.
    """
    P = _P("fl_shearography")
    vis = _shearo(shape, seed, P)             # cached — the SAME field, bit-exact
    drive = np.float32(P["drive"])
    hot = np.clip((vis - np.float32(0.62)) * np.float32(2.9), 0, 1)
    hot *= hot
    hot *= np.float32(0.40) * drive
    mod = vis * vis
    mod *= np.float32(0.34) * drive
    mod += hot
    mod += vis * drive
    mod += np.float32(0.46)
    mod = K.norm(mod)
    M = np.clip(15.0 + 34.0 * mod * sm, 0, 255)
    R = np.clip(196.0 - 74.0 * mod * sm, 15, 255)
    CC = np.clip(106.0 - 88.0 * mod * sm, 16, 255)
    return M.astype(np.float32), R.astype(np.float32), CC.astype(np.float32)

finishes.mechanism_summary:
Real shearography, built from its two actual optical stages rather than imitated. The draft's physics was right; its numbers were not, and both of its load-bearing failures were only visible by running the gate's own code.

STAGE 1 — objective speckle. A rough surface under coherent light returns a random walk of phasors, so the complex amplitude A = ar + i*ai is a band-limited GAUSSIAN field and the sensor records |A|^2 = ar*ar + ai*ai, a negative-exponential intensity: a dark ground with hot grains. Two band-limited noise fields are zero-meaned and box-blurred (the blur IS the imaging aperture, which is why it happens BEFORE the squaring), then squared and summed. The two lattices are incommensurate (g and 0.77g) because a single lattice left a faint square grid at exactly `grain`. Normalising by 2*mean instead of by max preserves the exponential tail so a few grains genuinely blow out. Measured: dropping the aperture blur raises GRIT from 0.069 to 0.109 and drops coherence from 0.647 to 0.534, so the blur stays — it is the difference between speckle and hash.

STAGE 2 — correlation fringes. Shearography measures w(x+dx) - w(x), so `surf - np.roll(surf, 16, axis=1)` is literally the shearing element. `surf` is a scatter of disbonds: a warped 210px folded-coordinate lattice of C1 polynomial domes (radius 76px), gated by a smooth field so only some sites have let go — the contract's own "fold the coordinate" trick, which replaced the draft's box-blurred noise blob (0.31s for a diamond-faceted bulge). The sheared difference of a round bulge is the classic two-lobed BUTTERFLY with a null down its middle. Specimen tilt adds the straight carrier: ph = k*(x cos a + y sin a) + gain*d, fringe brightness fr = 0.5 - 0.5 cos(ph), carrier angle hashed from seed. `gain` is normalised against the measured peak of d so `orders` means "fringe orders at the worst defect", and the steepest phase gradient at orders=8 is 0.74 rad/px — a 8.4px local period, above Nyquist with room.

The two stages multiply, each with its own pedestal: (0.08 + 0.92*fr) * (spkl + (1-spkl)*spk). With one shared pedestal the speckle (sd/mean ~1) buried the fringes and the finish read as flat cloth.

Colour: monochromatic illumination with an ADDITIVE emitted component, because a shearography monitor image is a sensor image, not darkened paint. The ground is the painter's colour times the correlation image; the emitted term (quadratic in the correlation image, plus the blown grains) is laid over it in the coherent line — their mean colour saturated, exposure-normalised, hue-rotated 0.42 rad via K.hue_rotate on a 1x1x3 array.

Why it fits the shelf's arc: the disbond is invisible to the eye and invisible in the paint's own contrast — it is ~150px across yet contributes almost nothing above 32px, appearing only as a bend in phase. The instrument is what makes it visible.
finishes.self_audit:
THE DRAFT FAILED TWO HARD GATES. I rebuilt it. Everything below is measured with the gate's own code (scripts/spb_finish_law.py scale_axis/follow_axis/coverage_axis and scripts/spb_variant_search.py measure), at the law's RES=1024 on its own flat 0.5-grey base, seed 51 — not a stub.

1. SCALE — DRAFT FAILED, 0.1907 vs a 0.20 floor. The draft's self-audit claimed 0.986, computed at 2048 against an 8-32px window. The law renders at RES=1024 and uses FIXED FFT bin radii (r=2048/32 and r=2048/8), so at 1024 the annulus is 4-16px OF THE RENDERED IMAGE. Features authored in absolute pixels do NOT shrink with render size, so the draft's 15px grain / 23px carrier landed at 23px rendered — outside the window, 80.6% of its energy in the coarse term. This is exactly the trap the assignment's "target feature px ~8" was warning about. Fixed by moving grain to 6-11px and the carrier to 8-14px. Measured now: MID paint_band 0.788 / spec_band 0.798, dominant peak 11.1px; LO 0.812 / 0.827, peak 8.1px; HI 0.826 / 0.833, peak 14.2px; both off-diagonal corners 0.724 and 0.881. Worst point in the whole SPACE is 0.724 against a 0.20 floor.

2. RENDER — DRAFT FAILED, 9.48s at 2048 (its self-audit claimed 1.5-2.0s from a stub whose _resize_array is not engine.core's). Profiled: box r=80 on the macro field 0.31s, K.px 0.17s, a float64 phase array from `pxc*np.cos(a)` promoting the whole canvas to 64-bit, and ~8 avoidable HxWx3 temporaries. Fixed by (a) replacing the blurred-noise disbond field with a folded-coordinate C1 dome lattice — no box at all, (b) np.arange broadcasting instead of K.px, so the tilt ramp is one add rather than four full-canvas arrays, (c) np.float32 scalars and out=/in-place everywhere, (d) three per-channel adds instead of one HxWx3 temp. Measured in a fresh process at 2048, paint+spec together: 0.77 / 1.14 / 1.19s. (Timings inside one long-lived process drift to 3-10s after repeated 2048 renders — that is this box's memory pressure, not the algorithm: the identical call measured 1.07s cold and 10.35s later in the same process, and a null incoming+finish tail drifted the same way.)

3. FOLLOW — the draft was already right in principle and I kept the construction, but the paint now has an additive emitted term, so `mod` rebuilds that too: 0.46 + drive*vis + 0.34*drive*vis^2 + 0.40*drive*hot, from the same K.cache entry (bit-identical, not merely similar). All three channels come off that one `mod`. The peak normaliser `bn` multiplies every paint term equally and so cancels exactly under K.norm — that is why it is absent from the spec. Measured amp_corr: 0.998 MID, 0.996 LO, 0.997 HI.

4. STORY / background — DRAFT STRADDLED A CELL BOUNDARY. Its CC = 96 - 52*mod put the median at 85.1, which is exactly the quantiser edge between cell 1 and cell 2, splitting the canvas 0.51/0.28 across two cells for no reason. Re-fitted to M = 15 + 34*mod*sm, R = 196 - 74*mod*sm, CC = 106 - 88*mod*sm. Measured medians on the law's base: 21.5 / 181.9 / 89.2 against the assigned 15 / 190 / 90 — inside +/-15 on all three (deltas 6.5 / 8.1 / 0.8), and at every corner of the SPACE (worst: 23.1 / 178.4 / 85.1). Dominant quantised cell (M0,R4,CC2) at 59%, with (0,3,1) 18% and (0,4,1) 17% on the ramp's tail. M cannot sit exactly on 15 because 15 is the floor of the ramp; +6.5 is the price of any metallic response in the hot grains. CC min is 18 at sm=1 (never below 16; the clip holds it at 16 at sm=2). richness_eff rose 1.8 -> 3.11.

5. COVERAGE / AMPLITUDE — dead 0.042 (MID), 0.024 (LO), 0.055 (HI), floor 0.70. sd/mean 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.56 against 0.10; band_abs 0.135 / 0.081 / 0.175 against 0.010 — the peak-normalised body and the additive emission roughly tripled band_abs versus the draft (0.048). Off the gate's grey base: white 0.15 dead (draft 0.47), cyan 0.00, maroon 0.43, near-black (0.04) 0.69 — that last one was 0.89 in the draft and is fixed by making the exposure normalisation real (the draft's max(c.max(), 0.25) floor defeated it exactly on the bases that needed it). Verified at pm 0/1/2 and sm 0/1/2.

6. NO CONFETTI — GRIT 0.050 MID, 0.096 LO, 0.033 HI (hard-fail at 0.62), neighbour coherence 0.64-0.71. The high-frequency content is a lattice-band-limited speckle multiplied by a continuous carrier, not hash. Nothing was added to pass a gate.

7. STRUCTURE / API — parsed with ast: no imports inside the block, no undefined names, only np.{arange,clip,cos,float32,floor,multiply,roll,sin} and K.{box,cache,finish,hue_rotate,incoming,mid,norm}, three module-level defs. paint_ starts from K.incoming and ends on K.finish(out, src, mask); verified with a partial mask that pixels outside it are returned untouched. spec_ returns three float32 arrays. Determinism verified: same seed with a cleared kit cache is bit-identical; a different seed differs. No Python loop anywhere except the 3-iteration channel add.

8. SPACE — 6 knobs, all read by the code, and the code reads nothing else (grepped): grain, pitch, orders, bond, spkl, drive. `drive` is the wide amplitude knob (0.45-1.55). I DROPPED the draft's `shear` knob: its own self-audit admitted the gain renormalisation makes it nearly inert, and a knob that does not change the look wastes a search dimension. It is now fixed at 16px in the source with the reason stated. `bond` replaces it and does change the look — measured, the gate area runs 0.86 -> 0.20 of dome sites across its range.

9. LOOKED AT IT AT 1:1, at 2048 and 1536, on grey / red / blue / gold bases, and at all three SPACE corners. It reads as a genuine shearogram: correlation fringes broken into speckle dashes, with unmistakable two-lobed butterfly fringe loops where a disbond has let go. The HI corner shows textbook closed fringe loops; the LO corner is a dense subtle speckle field. The disbonds are spread across the whole canvas (the draft's 320px macro field put them all on one side at 1024).

STILL FLAGGING, honestly:
  a. UNIQUENESS was NOT run — it needs the module assembled into the registry plus the catalog fingerprint index, which is the assembler's step, not mine. Specific concern, unchanged from the draft: away from the defects this is a regular diagonal fringe field that could rhyme structurally with a brushed / twill / hatched finish. What should save it is that the fringes are chopped into speckle dashes and curve into closed loops at every disbond, but that is judgement, not a measurement. Please run `python scripts/spb_uniqueness_gate.py --module engine.paint_v2.flaw_lab_2026` after assembly.
  b. A near-black base still lands at 0.69 dead — under the 0.70 gate but only just. This is inherent to any finish whose ground is the painter's colour; I have pushed it as far as the additive emitted term honestly allows.
  c. The macro layout is resolution-dependent in absolute pixels, as it is for every finish on this shelf: at 2048 there are ~95 dome sites and 20-65 active disbonds, at the law's 1024 about a quarter of that. It does not move any gate (coarse energy is 0.15-0.20 either way) but an audit thumbnail will show fewer butterflies than the shipped car.

# ══════════════════════════════════════ NN · HOLOGRAPHIC INTERFEROGRAM ══
# Second lattice: pitch 1.29x, rotated 31 deg. Folding ONE lattice returns its
# exact nearest point, so min() of two folds is an exact Voronoi F1 over their
# UNION for the cost of two folds instead of a 9-neighbour search - and two
# incommensurate lattices never repeat. The first cut used a single fold and
# passed every gate at band 0.68 while the 1:1 sheet was wallpaper: identical
# bullseyes in rows, and the fold's four-fold symmetry printing the same little
# concentric diamond at every cell corner. Warping harder never touched it (a
# warp moves a symmetric pattern, it does not break the symmetry).
_HI_RATIO, _HI_COS, _HI_SIN = 1.29, 0.85749, 0.51459
_HI_DM = 0.40625      # exact period-mean of d*(0.5+0.5d^2) - see the DC note below
_HI_RC = 0.42         # chirp saturates at 0.42*cell_px, so rim_px is a hard FLOOR
_HI_RMAX = 0.7071     # largest fold radius possible (cell corner of lattice 1)


def _holo_interfero(shape, seed, P):
    """Double-exposure holographic interferometry of a bulging skin disbond.

    A hologram of the part at rest is re-exposed with the part under load; the
    two reconstructions interfere and the fringe ORDER counts out-of-plane
    displacement in half-wavelength steps. A pressurised void under the skin
    bulges as a paraboloid, so t ~ r^2 and the fringe SPACING, 1/(dt/dr), goes as
    1/r - it SHRINKS OUTWARD. Every other ring field in this catalog is a uniform
    sin(d*f); the chirp IS the technique.

    GEOMETRY IS AUTHORED AS hub_px -> rim_px, NEVER AS COEFFICIENTS, and the
    chirp SATURATES. A pure paraboloid runs both ends out of the car window at
    once: measured on the un-clamped first cut, 6.9% of the canvas sat coarser
    than 32px at the wide corner of the space and 5.7% finer than 8px at the
    tight corner, and both ends are pure dilution to a RATIO gate. Here
    S = 1/hub_px pins the spacing at each bulge centre, B carries it down to
    1/rim_px at 0.42*cell_px, and past that radius the pitch is HELD - so rim_px
    is a floor, not a limit approached. Measured at 2048 over all ten sampled
    knob sets: spectral peak 15.2-23.0px, 87-95% of paint energy inside the
    8-32px window, 2.5-7.9% coarser than 32px.

    THE VISIBILITY TERMS MULTIPLY THE AC ONLY. Speckle and order decorrelation
    are real (a reconstruction is speckled, and high-order fringes wash out
    between exposures), but `dark` has a period-mean of _HI_DM, so scaling it by
    a slow envelope injects _HI_DM*d(envelope) of pure COARSE DC - the exact
    energy a RATIO gate counts against. Subtracting _HI_DM first makes the
    returned field zero-mean, so the envelope becomes amplitude modulation
    sitting beside the carrier instead of under it: measured pcoarse 0.069 ->
    0.048 on the same knobs. It is also why this finish now brightens as well as
    darkens - dead on a near-black base went 1.000 -> 0.424.

    Returns (sig, ordn): sig is the bipolar fringe signal, + on a constructive
    crest and - in a cancelled core; ordn is the normalised fringe ORDER.
    """
    h, w = shape[:2]

    def build():
        C = float(P["cell_px"])
        # One displacement of the whole plate at roughly the void size. K.warp is
        # octaves=2, so its own second octave supplies the finer wobble that keeps
        # the fringe outlines lumpy rather than drawn - a separate jitter pair
        # cost two more cached noise builds for the same look.
        wy, wx = K.warp(shape, seed + 31, 0.62 * C, 0.85 * C)

        def _fold2(qx, qy, cc):
            """SQUARED distance to the nearest point of a lattice of pitch cc.

            Squared, so the two lattices can be compared and only the winner
            takes the sqrt. Every step is in-place: a 2048^2 float32 temporary
            costs ~28ms of pure allocation on this box, measured against a 4.7ms
            hot multiply, and the whole finish is allocation-bound not FLOP-bound.
            """
            u = qx * np.float32(1.0 / cc)
            u -= np.floor(u)
            u -= np.float32(0.5)
            u *= u
            v = qy * np.float32(1.0 / cc)
            v -= np.floor(v)
            v -= np.float32(0.5)
            v *= v
            u += v
            u *= np.float32(cc * cc)
            return u

        ca, sa = np.float32(_HI_COS), np.float32(_HI_SIN)
        rx = wx * ca
        rx -= wy * sa
        ry = wx * sa
        ry += wy * ca
        r = np.minimum(_fold2(wx, wy, C), _fold2(rx, ry, C * _HI_RATIO))
        del rx, ry
        np.sqrt(r, out=r)

        rc = _HI_RC * C
        S = 1.0 / float(P["hub_px"])
        F = 1.0 / float(P["rim_px"])
        B = (F - S) / (2.0 * rc)
        rq = np.minimum(r, np.float32(rc))
        t = rq * np.float32(B)
        t += np.float32(S)
        t *= rq                                  # S*rq + B*rq^2 : the paraboloid
        r -= rq
        r *= np.float32(F)
        t += r                                   # held at the tightest pitch past rc
        del r, rq
        # Different voids hold different pressure, so they carry different fringe
        # counts. A SMOOTH field, not a per-cell lookup: a per-cell value jumps at
        # the cell wall and draws the lattice back in as a visible grid.
        bmul = K.mid(shape, 1.15 * C, seed + 13, octaves=2) * np.float32(0.28)
        bmul += np.float32(0.86)
        t *= bmul
        del bmul

        # The order an analyst writes on the print, normalised on the largest
        # radius the union can produce.
        nmax = S * rc + B * rc * rc + F * (_HI_RMAX * C - rc)
        ordn = t * np.float32(1.0 / max(nmax, 1e-3))
        np.clip(ordn, 0, 1, out=ordn)

        # Two-beam intensity is cos^2(phi/2), so the dark fringe locus is
        # sin^2(pi*t); the cubic tightens the cores the way a hard-printed
        # negative does. A polynomial and not a gamma because np.power with a
        # float exponent measured 33ms against 5ms for the equivalent multiply.
        t *= np.float32(2.0 * np.pi)
        d = np.cos(t, out=t)
        d *= np.float32(-0.5)
        d += np.float32(0.5)
        dark = d * d
        dark *= np.float32(0.5)
        dark += np.float32(0.5)
        dark *= d
        del d, t

        vis = ordn * np.float32(-0.42)           # high orders decorrelate
        vis += np.float32(1.0)
        spk = K.mid(shape, 12.0, seed + 77, octaves=1) * np.float32(0.22)
        spk += np.float32(0.78)                  # laser speckle: 12px and coherent
        vis *= spk
        del spk

        sig = np.float32(_HI_DM) - dark          # zero-mean BEFORE the envelope
        sig *= vis
        return sig, ordn

    return K.cache(("holoint", h, w, int(seed), _k(P)), build)


def paint_fl_holo_interfero(paint, shape, mask, seed, pm, bb):
    """Bright constructive crests and cancelled dark cores about the painter's own
    tone, packing tighter the further they run from each bulge centre."""
    P = _P("fl_holo_interfero")
    src = K.incoming(paint, shape)
    sig, ordn = _holo_interfero(shape, seed, P)

    g = sig * np.float32(1.30 * float(P["depth"]) * float(pm))
    g += np.float32(1.0)
    np.clip(g, 0.05, 1.85, out=g)

    m01 = sig * np.float32(1.35)
    m01 += np.float32(0.5)
    np.clip(m01, 0, 1, out=m01)
    m01 *= g

    # The reconstruction is monochromatic - one laser line - but these are BASE
    # finishes, so the line is derived FROM the painter's colour instead of
    # imposed on it. K.hue_rotate turns about the grey axis and preserves r+g+b
    # exactly, so neither line carries luminance structure of its own: crests
    # take the reconstructing line, cancelled cores fall back to the undiffracted
    # ground, and a blue car reconstructs blue. Rotating the MEAN colour keeps the
    # colour stage off the 3-channel broadcast path, which measured 1120ms against
    # 190ms for the per-channel form below.
    mc = src.reshape(-1, 3).mean(0).reshape(1, 1, 3)
    T = min(0.80, float(P["tint"]) * float(pm))
    c_hi = K.hue_rotate(mc, 0.62)[0, 0]
    c_lo = K.hue_rotate(mc, -0.85)[0, 0]

    gA = g * np.float32(1.0 - T)
    chans = []
    for c in range(3):
        lo = np.float32(float(c_lo[c]) * T)
        dv = np.float32((float(c_hi[c]) - float(c_lo[c])) * T)
        ch = src[:, :, c] * gA
        ch += g * lo
        ch += m01 * dv
        chans.append(ch)
    return K.finish(np.dstack(chans), src, mask)


def spec_fl_holo_interfero(shape, seed, sm, base_m, base_r):
    """GRAMMAR: ring-order ladder.

    The print is density-sliced - the analyst's isodensity read of a fringe
    negative - so each fringe resolves into flat contour bands with no grain in
    them at all. The second ladder is the ORDER itself: because visibility decays
    with order, how deep a ring is allowed to cut is set by WHICH ring it is.
    Ring one bottoms out on the lowest material, ring eight barely leaves the
    ground. Both ladders quantise the SAME `sig` the paint modulated with, and
    all three channels come off the one scalar `d`, so the spec cannot drift off
    the paint's geometry: measured amp_corr 0.945-0.987 across the whole space,
    both strength knobs and four base colours.

    Only the CUT side is laddered. `sig` is bipolar, so keying the material off it
    directly puts the washed-out high-order plate in the MIDDLE of the ladder
    instead of on the plate's own card, and the background cell fell to 0.20 of
    the canvas at steps=7 - a different finish's identity. Clipping at the crest
    side says what the technique says: the interfringe ground and the washed-out
    region are the SAME bare plate, and only fringe cores cut into it.

    BACKGROUND M/R/CC = 75/35/18, a bleached silver-halide holographic plate:
    residual silver leaves it half metallic, the emulsion is polished glass-flat,
    the cover glass deep clear. Measured, that cell holds 0.47-0.55 of the canvas
    on every one of the ten sampled knob sets - four times the next card - with
    7-8 cards dealt and an effective richness of 4.3-5.3.
    """
    P = _P("fl_holo_interfero")
    sig, ordn = _holo_interfero(shape, seed, P)

    cut = sig * np.float32(-1.242)
    cut += np.float32(0.262)
    np.clip(cut, 0, 1, out=cut)
    d = K.ladder(cut, int(P["steps"]), 0.0, 1.0)
    d *= K.ladder(ordn, 5, 1.0, 0.48)            # ring 1 cuts deep, ring 8 barely
    d *= np.float32(sm)

    M = d * np.float32(-68.0)
    M += np.float32(75.0)
    np.clip(M, 0, 255, out=M)
    R = d * np.float32(158.0)
    R += np.float32(35.0)
    np.clip(R, 15, 255, out=R)
    CC = d * np.float32(104.0)
    CC += np.float32(18.0)
    np.clip(CC, 16, 255, out=CC)
    return M, R, CC

finishes.mechanism_summary: A double-exposure hologram of a skin panel with pressurised disbonds under it. Fringe order t counts out-of-plane displacement in half-wavelength steps and a void bulges as a paraboloid, so the local fringe SPACING shrinks as you move outward from each bulge centre — the chirp is the point, against a catalog whose every other ring field is a uniform-spacing sin(d*f). Geometry is authored as hub_px -> rim_px and the chirp SATURATES: S = 1/hub_px pins the spacing at the centre, B carries it to 1/rim_px at 0.42*cell_px, and past that radius the pitch is held, so rim_px is a hard floor rather than a limit approached — that clamp is what keeps both ends of the chirp inside the 8-32px car window (measured 87-95% of paint energy in band, spectral peak 15.2-23.0px, on all ten sampled knob sets). The voids are the nearest seed of the UNION of two folded lattices, one at pitch C and one rotated 31 deg and scaled 1.29x, because folding a lattice returns its exact nearest point, so a minimum of two folds is an exact Voronoi F1 for the cost of two folds and two incommensurate lattices never repeat. Fringe visibility (laser speckle at 12px, plus order-dependent decorrelation) multiplies the AC ONLY: the fringe profile has an exact period-mean of 0.40625, so that mean is subtracted BEFORE the envelope is applied, turning what would be pure coarse DC at the void scale into amplitude modulation beside the carrier (pcoarse 0.069 -> 0.048), and making the finish brighten as well as darken. Colour: the reconstruction is monochromatic, so two laser lines are derived from the painter's own mean colour by K.hue_rotate — which preserves r+g+b exactly and therefore adds zero luminance structure — with constructive crests taking the reconstructing line and cancelled cores falling back to the undiffracted ground, so the painter's base still reads on red, grey, black and white.

The draft was NOT correct. It failed the RENDER gate outright and had four further defects I measured and fixed. Everything below is a number from a run, not an estimate.

(1) RENDER BUDGET — the draft FAILED. Stage profile at 2048 showed the draft allocating a fresh 16.8MB temporary at every step (a cold 2048^2 float32 op costs ~28ms of allocation against a 4.7ms hot multiply on this box): field builder 1298ms, paint colour stage 1120ms, K.finish 758ms, spec 687ms. Isolated best-of-4 cold render 1.64s, degrading to 3.38s and 3.92s on repeats, and 6.55s inside the gate harness — over the 3s gate. Its self_audit claimed 1.14s; that did not reproduce. FIX: every stage rewritten in-place, one sqrt instead of two (compare squared fold distances, root only the winner), the separate jitter noise pair dropped (K.warp is already octaves=2, its own second octave does that job), and the colour blend moved off the (H,W,1)x(H,W,3) broadcast path onto a 3-iteration per-channel loop — 1120ms -> ~190ms. RESULT, interleaved in ONE process against two shipped WRAP SHOP finishes as controls: fl_holo_interfero best 1.04s / median 1.85s; wrap_microbubble 1.18 / 1.53; wrap_print_band 1.30 / 1.76. Isolated best-of-4: 0.79s. It now sits inside the shipped band, and no run exceeded 1.92s.

(2) COARSE DC LEAK (SCALE). The draft multiplied `dark` by the visibility envelope. `dark` has an exact period-mean of 0.40625, so that injects 0.40625*delta(vis) of pure COARSE DC at the ~300px void scale — the exact energy a RATIO gate counts against. FIX: subtract the analytic mean first so the field is zero-mean and the envelope becomes AM beside the carrier. Measured pcoarse 0.069 -> 0.048, pband 0.906 -> 0.940 on the same knobs.

(3) UNBOUNDED CHIRP. The draft's paraboloid ran out of the window at both ends: measured 6.9% of the canvas coarser than 32px at the wide corner and 5.7% finer than 8px at the tight corner (lambda p1 6.6px there). Its self_audit claimed 96.5% between 10 and 30px; the honest number was 92.6-94.4% in 8-32px. FIX: C1 saturation at 0.42*cell_px makes rim_px a floor. Now E(>32px) 0.025-0.079 and E(<8px) 0.008-0.027 over all ten samples.

(4) DEAD ON DARK BASES. The draft only darkened (max gain 0.98), so a near-black base measured dead = 1.000 — a COVERAGE fail on that base. FIX: bipolar gain about 1.0 (bright constructive crest, dark cancelled core), which is also what two-beam interference actually does. dead 1.000 -> 0.424.

(5) SPEC BACKGROUND NOT DOMINANT ACROSS THE SPACE — a requirement-4 miss. At the fine corner (steps=7) the draft's dominant cell was (1,1,0) at 0.276 with the assigned 75/35/18 cell down at 0.201. FIX: ladder only the CUT side of the bipolar signal, so the interfringe ground and the washed-out high-order plate land on the SAME card. Measured dominant cell now (1,0,0) at exactly M/R/CC = 75/35/18, holding 0.468-0.553 on every one of the ten points the search will actually sample — four to six times the next card. Two smaller fixes: nmax used 0.68*C where the true max fold radius is 0.7071*C (measured r.max/C = 0.706), and cell_px 230-370 made the organiser ~300px, a poster rather than a field — now 150-265, and the whole-canvas view is an even allover field with no grid and no dead corners.

MEASURED GATE RESULTS, FINISH LAW code called directly (scale_axis / follow_axis / coverage_axis) plus the variant harness's own measure(), at 2048 on all ten sampled knob sets and on pm=2, sm=0, sm=2, four base colours and two seeds: pband 0.872-0.948 (SCALE floor 0.20), sband 0.827-0.856, amp_corr 0.945-0.987 (FOLLOW floor 0.35), dead 0.000-0.549 (ceiling 0.70), band 0.522-0.728, grit 0.011-0.036, amp 0.179-0.637 (floor 0.065), band_abs 0.0256-0.1199 (floor 0.010), contrast 0.114-0.611 (floor 0.06), cover 1.00, shades 0.33-0.41, richness_eff 4.30-5.27 (Brass Night, the owner's DARK CITY winner, is 4.6), 7-8 material cells at >=1%. Spectral peak 15.2-23.0px; 18.6px at the shipped midpoint.

STRUCTURAL CHECKS, run by AST against the block and then live inside the real flaw_lab_2026 template: parses; zero imports in the block; zero unresolved names; K.* used = cache/finish/hue_rotate/incoming/ladder/mid/warp (all real); np.* used = clip/cos/dstack/float32/floor/minimum/pi/sqrt (all real); exactly one loop, `for c in range(3)` over colour channels, no exp/sin in it; SPACE knobs and the knobs the code reads match exactly, 6 of them, with depth (0.45, 1.30) as the wide amplitude knob; module imports and install() wires paint_fn + base_spec_fn; paint returns float32 in 0.024..0.589 all finite and ends on K.finish(out, src, mask) after starting from K.incoming; spec returns three float32 arrays with CC min 18.0 (never below 16); identical output for the same seed, different for seed 8, mask respected outside the mask; and the cached (sig, ordn) shared by paint and spec is provably never mutated by either.

I ALSO LOOKED AT IT. 1:1 crops and a whole-canvas view: irregular bullseyes of differing size, adjacent ones running together the way real disbonds do, ring spacing visibly tightening outward, hyperbolic saddles between neighbours, no wallpaper repeat, no confetti, painter's base colour clearly reading through. The spec crop shows flat quantised contour bands with zero grain, sitting exactly on the paint's rings.

WHAT I AM STILL UNSURE ABOUT. Three things. First, the whole-catalog UNIQUENESS gate needs the finish installed in the registry plus a fingerprint refresh — the integrating agent's step. The argument for why it should clear is that a chirp on an aperiodic seed set has a broad spatial spectrum where an existing uniform sin(d*f) ring field's is narrow, but that is an argument, not a measurement. Second, STORY is a shelf ratio and cannot be computed with one finish present; what I can say is that the background cell is (1,0,0) at exactly 75/35/18 and is dominant on every sample. Third, a white painter base measures dead = 0.549 — under the ceiling, but the constructive crests clip; that is what a hologram crest does and I left it, though it is the one base colour where a painter will see blown highlights. A minor look risk remains at fold saddles between two voids, which produce nested hyperbolic fringes: physically correct and now irregular rather than gridded, but a few read as small nested diamonds at 1:1. Timing on this machine also has real allocator variance (identical cold renders measured 0.79, 0.81, 1.10 and 1.90s), so the margin against the 3s gate is roughly 1.6x on the median, not 3x.

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════ 07 · ULTRASONIC C-SCAN ══
def _cscan_gate(shape, seed, P):
    """The gated echo amplitude of a raster ultrasonic scan, as the instrument draws it.

    A C-scan is not a picture of the part. A transducer is dragged across it under a
    couplant film, one pass at a time, and the gate keeps ONE number per probe
    POSITION — the height of the echo returning from inside. So the image inherits the
    SCAN's geometry, not the part's: one flat cell per trigger, stepped at the pass
    pitch in y and the encoder step in x, serrated wherever the sweep reversed, and
    blank wherever the couplant broke and nothing came back at all.

    Every raster term (pass index, rule profile, parity, per-pass gain) is a COLUMN
    of shape (h,1), so the cos() below runs over 2048 elements rather than 4.2M — the
    dominant structure of this finish is nearly free to build.
    """
    h, w = shape[:2]

    def build():
        pitch = float(P["pitch"])
        rows = np.arange(h, dtype=np.float32)[:, None] * np.float32(1.0 / pitch)
        line = np.floor(rows)                       # which pass this row belongs to
        frac = rows - line                          # where inside the pass it sits
        rng = np.random.default_rng((int(seed) * 2654435761 + 0x5CA9) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        gl = rng.random(int(h / pitch) + 3, dtype=np.float32)
        gain_l = gl[line.astype(np.int32)]          # this pass's coupling / gain
        # The plotted raster rule, as a RAISED COSINE. Measured: a hard-edged rule of
        # 0.30 duty put its 2nd harmonic at pitch/2 = 7.5px, i.e. BELOW the 8px window,
        # where it is pure dilution — the spec's spectral peak landed at 7.5px. A raised
        # cosine is a single spectral line exactly at the pass pitch and nothing else,
        # which is why this finish's peak sits at 10-16px on every SPACE sample.
        ink = 0.5 + 0.5 * np.cos(frac * np.float32(2.0 * np.pi))
        par = np.mod(line, 2.0) * 2.0 - 1.0         # bidirectional sweep parity
        # What the probe is looking at: through-thickness attenuation. Disbonds and
        # porosity are hand-sized on a car panel (~150px) and can NEVER be allowed to
        # touch luminance directly — see the AM trick in `tone`. The 9px octave exists
        # only to be point-sampled once per probe cell, which turns it into honest
        # cell-to-cell grain scatter rather than any visible 9px texture.
        A = K.norm(0.55 * K.mid(shape, 150.0, seed + 11, octaves=3)
                   + 0.27 * K.mid(shape, 39.0, seed + 12, octaves=2)
                   + 0.18 * K.mid(shape, 9.0, seed + 13, octaves=1))
        # ONE sample per probe position, held across the whole cell. This gather IS the
        # instrument: it is what makes a smooth attenuation field come out as a lattice
        # of flat square cells at the scan pitch instead of a smooth blob.
        yi = np.clip((line + 0.5) * pitch, 0, h - 1).astype(np.int32)
        xc = np.arange(w, dtype=np.float32)[None, :] * np.float32(1.0 / pitch)
        xs = np.clip((np.floor(xc) + 0.5) * pitch, 3.0, w - 4.0).astype(np.int32)
        # Encoder lag on the reverse sweep offsets alternate passes by 3px, so every
        # palette boundary comes out serrated at exactly the pass pitch. It is the
        # artefact that dates a real C-scan.
        xi = xs + (par * 3.0).astype(np.int32)
        att = A[yi, xi]
        g = float(P["gain"])
        # Coupling gain rides the amplitude BEFORE the gate quantises it, so the palette
        # walks a step or two between neighbouring passes — the line banding every
        # operator knows on sight.
        echo = np.clip(1.62 * (att - 0.5) + 0.5 + g * 0.24 * (gain_l - 0.5), 0, 1)
        disp = K.ladder(echo, int(P["steps"]), 0.0, 1.0)     # the display's palette
        # Coupling loss shows up first where the echo was already weak: a starved pass
        # goes blank for the run where it crosses a low-return region.
        drop = ((gain_l < 0.075) & (att < 0.44)).astype(np.float32)
        # THE WHOLE LUMINANCE STORY, and it is deliberately built out of the raster.
        # The plotter modulates LINE WEIGHT per palette level, so the 150px amplitude
        # map reaches luminance only as an AMPLITUDE MODULATION of the pass-pitch
        # carrier — energy at f_c +/- f_m, still inside the car window. Measured: the
        # first cut drove luminance off the map directly and scored paint_band 0.077
        # with its spectral peak at 683px; carrying the same information as AM of the
        # rule takes it to 0.50-0.72 with the peak at the pitch.
        tone = ((1.0 - float(P["rule"]) * (0.30 + 0.70 * disp) * ink)
                * (1.0 + 0.055 * g * par)           # forward vs reverse sweep gain
                * (0.90 + 0.20 * gain_l)            # per-pass coupling drift
                * (1.0 - 0.55 * drop))              # dropout runs
        return disp.astype(np.float32), tone.astype(np.float32)

    return K.cache(("c_scan", h, w, int(seed), _k(P)), build)


def paint_fl_c_scan(paint, shape, mask, seed, pm, bb):
    """A gated amplitude map painted by a raster scan, in the instrument's palette."""
    P = _P("fl_c_scan")
    src = K.incoming(paint, shape)
    disp, tone = _cscan_gate(shape, seed, P)
    p = float(pm)
    wgt = np.float32([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722])
    # FALSE COLOUR THAT IS EXACTLY ISOLUMINANT. K.hue_rotate turns about the RGB grey
    # axis, which is NOT luma-neutral under Rec709 — measured, rotating a livery red
    # dumped the entire 150px amplitude map into luminance (81% of the paint's energy
    # coarse). Subtracting the rotated luma leaves a pure zero-luma chroma vector, so
    # amplitude lives in HUE, the raster keeps the contrast, and the painter's own
    # colour stays the axis the palette turns about.
    rot = K.hue_rotate(src, (disp - 0.45) * (float(P["span"]) * p))
    l0 = src @ wgt
    chroma = rot - (rot @ wgt)[:, :, None]
    # A rotation cannot colour an achromatic livery — a white car came back as bare
    # raster lines. So the palette also EMITS the NDT cold/hot opponent, along the
    # (1, -0.1963, -1) direction whose Rec709 luma is exactly zero, small enough that a
    # coloured base still owns the hue.
    e = (float(P["emit"]) * p) * (disp - 0.45)
    # The readout is a printed film, and it carries its own density — without it a
    # near-black livery multiplies to nothing and band_abs fails. Dark bases get the
    # most print, light bases the least, so a white car never clips its raster flat.
    lift = 0.14 * (1.0 - 0.55 * l0)
    lum = (l0 * (1.0 - 0.16 * p) + p * lift) * (1.0 + p * (tone - 1.0))
    out = lum[:, :, None] + chroma * (1.0 + p * (0.95 * disp - 0.42))[:, :, None]
    out[:, :, 0] += e
    out[:, :, 1] -= 0.1963 * e
    out[:, :, 2] -= e
    return K.finish(out, src, mask)


def spec_fl_c_scan(shape, seed, sm, base_m, base_r):
    """GRAMMAR: hard colormap ladder. The readout owns a fixed palette, so every channel
    is cut into discrete material steps off the one displayed field — 11 / 14 / 9 levels
    plus a 5-level substrate ladder, no two sharing a step boundary, and no grain.

    Material story: a dry couplant/print film over the panel (M10 R200 CC200 — the
    dominant cell at 0.70 of canvas), slicker where the ink went down dense on a strong
    return, and as-rolled mill-finish panel showing through the unprinted rules and the
    dropout runs (M to 184, ~3% of canvas — the second material).
    """
    P = _P("fl_c_scan")
    disp, tone = _cscan_gate(shape, seed, P)
    # FOLLOW by construction: because every colour operation above is exactly
    # zero-luma, the paint's luminance IS `tone`, so cutting all three channels from it
    # is not an analogy, it is the same field. Measured amp_corr 0.93-0.99.
    # The affine is PARAMETRIC, not K.norm: `rule` sets both where tone sits and how far
    # it spreads (fitted, median = 1 - 0.34*rule to within 0.006 over the whole SPACE),
    # and K.norm would have let the dropout runs drag the canvas off the assigned
    # background. With it, the spec median is 12/197/200 on all ten SPACE samples.
    rule = float(P["rule"])
    mod = np.clip(0.5 + (tone - (1.0 - 0.34 * rule)) / (0.16 + 1.30 * rule), 0, 1)
    bare = np.clip((0.155 - mod) * 7.0, 0, 1)          # unprinted substrate
    M = np.clip(10.0 + (K.ladder(1.0 - mod, 11, -22.0, 26.0)
                        + K.ladder(bare, 5, 0.0, 148.0)) * sm, 0, 255)
    R = np.clip(200.0 + K.ladder(mod, 14, 44.0, -44.0) * sm, 15, 255)
    CC = np.clip(200.0 + K.ladder(mod, 9, 34.0, -34.0) * sm, 16, 255)
    return M.astype(np.float32), R.astype(np.float32), CC.astype(np.float32)

finishes.mechanism_summary: Ultrasonic C-scan imaging, built as the SCAN rather than as the flaw. A through-thickness attenuation map (150px disbonds + 39px porosity + a 9px scatter octave) is sampled ONCE per probe position and held flat across the whole cell, so the picture is a lattice of square C-scan pixels at the scan pitch in BOTH axes, not a smooth map; alternate passes are swept the other way, so encoder lag offsets them by 3px and serrates every palette boundary at exactly that pitch. Per-pass coupling gain rides the amplitude before the gate quantises it, so the palette walks a step or two between neighbouring passes — the line banding every operator recognises. A starved pass goes blank for the run where it crosses a low-return region (dropout). The plotted raster rule is a raised cosine, a single spectral line at the pass pitch with no harmonics below the 8px floor, and the plotter modulates its LINE WEIGHT per palette level — so the necessarily-coarse 150px amplitude map reaches luminance only as amplitude modulation of that in-band carrier, never directly. False colour is an exactly isoluminant hue rotation of the painter's own colour (the rotated luma is subtracted, leaving a pure zero-luma chroma vector) plus an emitted cold/hot opponent along the zero-luma (1, -0.1963, -1) direction, so an achromatic livery still gets a map. Because every colour operation is zero-luma, the paint's luminance IS the raster field `tone`, and the spec cuts all three channels from that same field into hard palette ladders: dry couplant/print film at M10/R200/CC200, slicker where the ink went down dense, and as-rolled mill-finish panel (M to 184) through the unprinted rules and dropout runs.
finishes.self_audit:
THE DRAFT WAS NOT CORRECT. I built it as a probe, measured it against the real gate maths (RES-independent FFT bins 64/256, copied from spb_finish_law.py), found three real defects and one fabricated audit, and rewrote it. All numbers below are measured, not reasoned.

(1) SCALE — the draft's PAINT was a coarse colour blob and only passed because the gate takes max(paint_band, spec_band). Measured over its 10 SPACE samples at 1024: paint_band 0.077-0.121, and at 2048 its radial spectral peak was 683 px with 81% of paint energy in the coarse bin. Its own self-audit claimed "paint band 0.33-0.43" — that was false. Proof of cause: rendering the identical draft on a WHITE base (where a hue rotation is a no-op) jumped paint_band from 0.121 to 0.361, so the coarse energy came entirely from the hue rotation and the grey-axis saturation ladder pushing the 150px amplitude map into luminance. K.hue_rotate turns about the RGB grey axis, which is NOT luma-neutral under the Rec709 weights the gate uses.
    FIX, two parts. (a) Colour is now exactly isoluminant — the rotated luma is subtracted to leave a zero-luma chroma vector, saturation scales that vector (so it cannot move luma), and the emitted opponent runs along (1, -0.1963, -1) whose Rec709 luma is exactly zero. (b) The amplitude map reaches luminance ONLY as amplitude modulation of the pass-pitch carrier, because the plotter modulates line weight per palette level: (1 - rule*(0.30+0.70*disp)*ink). AM of an in-band carrier by a slow envelope puts its energy at f_c ± f_m, still in the window. Result over 10 samples: paint_band 0.496-0.722, spec_band 0.496-0.699, spectral peak 10-16 px on every sample (floor 0.20).

(2) FOLLOW — the draft measured 0.491-0.701, not the claimed 0.737-0.856. It passed, but only by luck: the paint's luminance was contaminated by hue/saturation terms the spec never saw. Now that every colour op is zero-luma, the paint's luminance IS `tone` and the spec cuts M, R and CC from that identical field. Measured 0.954-0.993 across the SPACE, and 0.931-0.966 on near-black / white / blue / gold bases.

(3) BACKGROUND — the draft's spec median drifted from 10/192/198 to 17/210/208 across the SPACE because it used a FIXED affine while `rule` shifts tone's median. I fitted the drift instead: median(tone) = 1 - 0.34*rule to within 0.006 over the whole range, spread = 0.16 + 1.30*rule. With the parametric affine the spec median is 12.0 / 196.6 / 200.0 on ALL TEN samples, dominant quantised cell (0,4,4) at 0.69-0.74 of canvas — the assigned 10/200/200. Bare mill-finish metal is the second material at 2.4-3.5% of canvas (M to 184), so 5 cells clear the 1% STORY floor.

(4) A CONTRACT VIOLATION the draft's audit did not mention: at pm=0 it still applied `col = grey + (col-grey)*(0.62+0.92*disp)` with no `p` factor, so a user strength of 0 permanently desaturated the paint. The contract says multiply the modulation by pm, never the base level. Measured on the corrected version: pm=0 returns the base colour with max|deviation| = 0.00000.

(5) I RETRACT ONE OF MY OWN EARLY FINDINGS. Raw wall-clock at 2048 said the draft took 6.5-7.5s and my rewrite 5-13s — both apparent budget failures. # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ A-SCAN GATE ══
_ASCAN_TRIG = 0.62      # gate trigger: the fraction of full screen height an echo
                        # must reach before the instrument calls it a hit
_ASCAN_PHASE = 2.05     # radians the trace phosphor sits off the painter's colour
_ASCAN_GA = 0.30        # flaw gate, centred at this fraction of the sweep
_ASCAN_GB = 0.66        # backwall gate — the two brackets the operator sets
_ASCAN_GW = 0.055       # gate half-width, as a fraction of the sweep


def _ascan(shape, seed, P):
    """Ultrasonic pulse-echo, stacked trace by trace — how a B-scan is built.

    X is TIME OF FLIGHT and Y is trace number, so one row band IS one A-scan.
    The probe fires, the wall reverberates, and echoes come back at equal
    intervals dying away until the next pulse re-triggers the sweep. Wall
    thickness and probe lift-off both shift the whole train in time, so every
    trace arrives a little early or late — that jitter is what turns a 1-D
    waveform into an image. The gate cursors do NOT move with it: they sit on
    the instrument's clock, which is exactly why a shifted echo falls out of
    gate.

    Costed deliberately: everything that is a function of TIME ONLY (the sweep
    sawtooth, the transmit pulse, both gates and their rules) is built as a
    (1,w) ROW and everything that is a function of TRACE only as an (h,1)
    COLUMN, so only six fields are ever materialised full-canvas. Building
    those as HxW first measured 4.67x the shelf's reference finish at 2048;
    broadcasting them is 2.45x, for identical pixels (max |diff| 9e-8).
    """
    h, w = shape[:2]

    def build():
        pitch = float(P["pitch"])
        sweep = float(P["sweep"])
        th = max(2, int(round(float(P["trace"]))))
        # ---- (1,w): the instrument's own clock. NEVER jittered — the traces
        # wander, the time base does not, and that contrast is the whole idea.
        xr = np.arange(w, dtype=np.float32)[None, :]
        s = xr - sweep * np.floor(xr * (1.0 / sweep))      # time since the pulse
        nm = s * (1.0 / pitch)                             # echoes elapsed
        dp = np.minimum(s, sweep - s)
        pulse = 1.6 - dp * (1.6 / (0.018 * sweep))         # transmit pulse, off-scale
        gh = _ASCAN_GW * sweep
        de = np.minimum(np.abs(s - _ASCAN_GA * sweep), np.abs(s - _ASCAN_GB * sweep))
        gwin = (de < gh).astype(np.float32)                # the two gate windows
        grule = (np.abs(de - gh) < 2.2).astype(np.float32)  # their four cursor rules
        # ---- (h,1): per-TRACE arrival time, CONSTANT down a trace and stepping
        # at the next one. A streaked 2-D noise was tried first and read as smooth
        # pinstripes on the 1:1 sheet; stepping per trace is what makes the field
        # read as stacked waveforms, and it is nearly free.
        rows = (np.arange(h, dtype=np.int32) // th) * th
        drift = K.mid((h, 4), 3.4 * th, seed + 17, octaves=1)[:, :1]   # wall thickness
        lift = K.mid((h, 4), 1.15 * th, seed + 23, octaves=1)[:, :1]   # probe lift-off
        jc = K.norm(0.64 * drift[rows] + 0.36 * lift[rows])
        # ---- the genuinely 2-D work
        t = xr + (jc - 0.5) * (2.0 * float(P["wobble"]) * pitch)
        # Disbond domains: sparse patches where the sound never reaches the far wall.
        fl = np.clip((K.mid((h, w), 110.0, seed + 29, octaves=1) - 0.58) * 4.5, 0, 1)
        # Fold the time axis — ONE pass draws every reverberation in the train.
        ad = np.abs(t - pitch * np.round(t * (1.0 / pitch)))
        hw = pitch * float(P["pfrac"])
        inv = 1.0 / (hw * hw)
        q = ad * ad * inv
        # Ricker wavelet (1-3.8u²)e^(-1.9u²) — the standard pulse-echo model, and
        # the reason the trough is 0.446 of the peak instead of the ~0.05 a squared
        # cosine gave: measured, and the dark ringing bands either side of each echo
        # were invisible on the sheet until this replaced it.
        rf = (1.0 - 3.8 * q) * np.exp(np.float32(-1.9) * q)
        # A disbond reflects from half the wall depth, so a SECOND train appears
        # interleaved between the wall echoes over the bad patches. Only its
        # amplitude is gated by `fl`; re-scaling the pitch instead was tried and
        # tore the echo phase at the domain edges — GRIT 0.010 -> 0.214, measured.
        d2 = ad - 0.5 * pitch
        q2 = d2 * d2 * inv
        rf += ((1.0 - 3.8 * q2) * np.exp(np.float32(-1.9) * q2)) * fl
        # Die-away, normalised so the last echo of a train is 26% of the first at
        # ANY sweep length; a disbond shadows the backwall, so the train dies
        # faster there. `an` is (1,w) — the whole envelope costs three HxW ops.
        an = (2.80 * pitch / sweep) * nm
        rf /= (1.0 + an * (1.0 + 1.6 * fl))
        # Couplant: transmission is best with the probe square to the surface and
        # falls off with tilt EITHER way, which bands the traces in Y.
        rf *= (1.0 - 1.10 * np.abs(jc - 0.5))
        rf = np.maximum(rf, pulse)
        # SOFT screen saturation, never a hard clip. Clipping at |1| with gain 1.5
        # flattened every echo to the same white and DELETED the die-away — the one
        # thing an A-scan exists to show. u/(1+|u|) is monotone, so a decayed echo
        # always draws dimmer than a fresh one at any gain.
        u = rf * float(P["gain"])
        mod = 0.5 + 0.5 * (u / (1.0 + np.abs(u)))
        return mod.astype(np.float32, copy=False), gwin, grule

    return K.cache(("ascan", h, w, int(seed), _k(P)), build)


def paint_fl_a_scan_gate(paint, shape, mask, seed, pm, bb):
    """The flaw detector's screen: a couplant-wet part written over with its own
    echo train and the box's gate graphics."""
    P = _P("fl_a_scan_gate")
    src = K.incoming(paint, shape)
    mod, gwin, grule = _ascan(shape, seed, P)
    sig = (mod - 0.5) * 2.0                                   # the signed RF trace
    pos = np.maximum(sig, 0.0)
    hit = np.clip((mod - _ASCAN_TRIG) * (1.0 / (1.0 - _ASCAN_TRIG)), 0, 1)
    # Three colours, all of them the painter's: the part, the phosphor the trace is
    # written in (their colour rotated about the grey axis), and the near-white ink
    # the box draws its own graphics in. Their base choice drives all three.
    avg = src[::8, ::8].reshape(-1, 3).mean(0).astype(np.float32)[None, None, :]
    trace = np.clip(K.hue_rotate(avg, _ASCAN_PHASE)[0, 0] * 1.25 + 0.12, 0, 1)
    ink = np.clip(trace * 0.30 + 0.72, 0, 1)
    # Alphas. EVERY modulation scales with pm, so pm=0 is the instrument switched
    # off and hands the part back flat (band 0.000, measured). The gate panel
    # SHADES the trace behind it, which is what makes a window read as an overlay
    # rather than as more stripes, and lets a trip inside one stand out.
    ga = np.clip((0.32 * pos + 0.80 * hit) * ((1.0 - 0.55 * gwin) * float(pm)), 0, 1)
    gb = np.clip(((0.95 * gwin) * hit + (0.16 * gwin + 0.62 * grule)) * float(pm), 0, 1)
    # The part reads dark and wet, the ringing troughs darker still. The couplant
    # film has its own low sheen, which is what keeps a near-black base off the
    # floor: without it a 0.03 base measured 78% DEAD, and 55% with it.
    dim = np.maximum(0.52 + (0.42 * float(pm)) * np.minimum(sig, 0.0), 0.05)
    film = 0.026 + (0.034 * float(pm)) * pos
    inv_gb = 1.0 - gb
    keep = (1.0 - ga) * inv_gb
    out = src * (dim * keep)[:, :, None]
    out += trace[None, None, :] * (ga * inv_gb)[:, :, None]
    out += ink[None, None, :] * gb[:, :, None]
    out += (film * keep)[:, :, None]
    return K.finish(out, src, mask)


def spec_fl_a_scan_gate(shape, seed, sm, base_m, base_r):
    """GRAMMAR: echo-spike duotone. The trigger splits the surface into exactly two
    materials — couplant-wet part below it, hard mirror metal above — each carrying
    its own rungs of a nine-step ladder, with the box's printed graphics stamped
    over both as a third, dead-flat gloss ink.

    All three channels are driven off ONE field, `drv`, rebuilt from the same
    `mod`/`gwin`/`grule` the paint used. Splitting them across different fields is
    what failed FOLLOW before: an earlier mapping drew the instrument ink BRIGHT in
    spec luma while the echoes drew dark, the two cancelled where they overlap, and
    amp_corr fell to 0.300 against a 0.35 floor. One driver, one sign: 0.77-0.84
    across all ten variants of the space.
    """
    P = _P("fl_a_scan_gate")
    mod, gwin, grule = _ascan(shape, seed, P)
    sh = K.ladder(mod, 9, 0.0, 1.0)                 # nine clean rungs, zero grain
    spike = (mod > _ASCAN_TRIG).astype(np.float32)
    lit = spike * sh                                # echo amplitude, in instrument steps
    ink = np.maximum(spike * gwin, grule)           # the rules, and the trips inside a gate
    drv = 16.0 * sh + 118.0 * lit + 34.0 * spike    # the one driver
    M = np.clip(45.0 + sm * (drv - 37.0 * ink), 0, 255)
    R = np.clip(160.0 - sm * (0.62 * drv + 120.0 * ink + 8.0 * gwin), 15, 255)
    CC = np.clip(40.0 - sm * (0.10 * drv + 9.0 * sh + 24.0 * ink), 16, 255)
    return (M.astype(np.float32, copy=False), R.astype(np.float32, copy=False),
            CC.astype(np.float32, copy=False))

finishes.mechanism_summary: Pulse-echo ultrasonics drawn the way the flaw detector draws it: X is time of flight, Y is trace number, so stacking A-scans line by line makes the B-scan image. Each sweep opens with an off-scale transmit pulse (a hard unjittered rule every `sweep` px), then the wall reverberates: one echo train is built by folding the time axis (`ad = |t - pitch*round(t/pitch)|`), which draws every backwall multiple in a single pass, each echo a Ricker wavelet (1-3.8u²)e^(-1.9u²) whose 0.446 trough gives the dark ringing bands either side of every bright return. Amplitude dies away hyperbolically across the sweep, normalised so the last echo is 26% of the first at any sweep length, and re-triggers at the next pulse. The train is replicated per TRACE, not per pixel: a row band of `trace` px is one A-scan, so the arrival time is constant down a trace and steps at the next one, driven by two 1-D noises — wall thickness (drifting over ~3.4 traces) and probe lift-off (~1.2 traces). Lift-off also costs coupling, so amplitude scales by (1 - 1.10|jit - 0.5|): best square to the surface, worse tilted either way, which bands the traces in Y. Sparse disbond domains insert a second train interleaved at half the wall depth and make the backwall behind them die faster. The display transfer is a soft saturation u/(1+|u|), monotone at any gain, so a decayed echo always draws dimmer than a fresh one — a hard clip erases the die-away, which is the only thing an A-scan exists to show. Two gates — a flaw window at 0.30 of the sweep and a backwall window at 0.66 — are drawn on the instrument's own unjittered clock, so their cursors are dead straight while the traces wander past them; each window shades the trace behind it like a real overlay panel, is bracketed by two hairline rules, and any echo that crosses the trigger inside one blazes to the alarm ink. Colour: the painter's base is the part under couplant, its hue rotated 117° about the grey axis is the trace phosphor, and a near-white lift is the box's printed ink — three colours, all derived from their base choice, plus a thin achromatic couplant sheen so a near-black base still reads as wet metal rather than a hole.

THE DRAFT WAS NOT CORRECT. It passed the mechanical axes but failed by eye and carried nine defects; I rebuilt it and re-measured everything. Ten faults found:

(1) HARD CLIP KILLED THE MECHANISM. `clip(rf*gain, -1, 1)` at gain 0.95-1.90 saturated every echo to the same white, so the die-away — the entire point of an A-scan — was invisible on the 1:1 sheet. Replaced with a monotone soft saturation u/(1+|u|). (2) The jitter was a streaked 2-D noise, which rendered as smooth PINSTRIPES, not stacked waveforms; it is now stepped per trace from two 1-D columns. (3) No transmit pulse, so nothing marked where a sweep began and the decay had no reference. (4) The gate cursors were indistinguishable from ordinary saturated echoes — the finish's own name did not read; each window now shades the trace behind it and is bracketed by rules. (5) `0.85*ged` was not multiplied by pm, so at pm=0 the cursor rules stayed burned in (measured band 0.561 at pm=0; now 0.000). (6) `sm` was applied only to `spike`, so at sm=0 the spec still carried structure in CC and on `hot`; now every modulation scales with sm and sm=0 returns a flat 45/160/40. (7) COVERAGE: on a 0.03 base the draft was 78.5% DEAD (fail line 0.70) because it only multiplied the source; a couplant-sheen floor brings it to 0.552. The draft's claim that it "works on ... black" was false. (8) FOLLOW was fragile, not robust: my first re-spec drew the instrument ink BRIGHT in spec luma while the echoes drew dark, the two cancelled where they overlap, and amp_corr fell to 0.300 on the variant the search then CHOSE. Fixed by driving all three channels off one signed driver `drv` — 0.771-0.838 across all ten. (9) PERFORMANCE: the draft built every time-only field (sweep sawtooth, gates, rules) full-canvas, measuring 4.67x the contract's reference finish timed paired in one process, with a median over the 3s budget; those are now (1,w) rows and (h,1) columns, giving 2.45x for bit-identical output (max |diff| 9e-8). The draft's claim of "1.8x the shipping reference" did not survive a paired measurement. (10) The SPACE let the search pick variants I would not ship: `shift` was absolute px so at pitch 15/shift 12 the wobble was 75% of a period, and the search's grit penalty drove it to wobble 0.10 (plain pinstripes) and gain 1.07 (invisible trace). `shift` is now `wobble`, a fraction of pitch, and the box is tightened so every sample is shippable. I also reverted one of my own "optimisations": modulating the pitch by the disbond field saved 10 ops and one np.exp but tore the echo phase at the domain edges — GRIT 0.010 -> 0.214. Physics, not op count, decided it.

(a) DOMINANT FEATURE SIZE — the echo interval `pitch`, 15-26 px (midpoint 20). That is the repeat carrying all the contrast: a ~5 px bright core, a ~5 px dark ringing trough each side, next echo 20 px away. Nothing larger carries real contrast — the sweep (260-460 px), the gate panels and the 110 px disbond domains only MODULATE the amplitude of that zero-mean carrier (the Ricker integrates to exactly zero, so an envelope produces sidebands, not DC). Measured, not asserted: the LAW's own SCALE axis (FFT annulus / total, from scripts/spb_finish_law.py) reads max(band_paint, band_spec) = 0.344-0.459 at the law's 1024 canvas and 0.53-0.62 at 2048, against a 0.20 floor, across all ten variants.

(b) EXACT EXPRESSION THE SPEC RECONSTRUCTS — nothing is rebuilt: `spec_` calls the identical cached `_ascan(shape, seed, P)` and reads the same three returned fields. `sh = K.ladder(mod, 9, 0, 1)`, `spike = mod > 0.62` (the same trigger the paint's `hit` ramp starts at), `lit = spike*sh`, `ink = max(spike*gwin, grule)` — exactly the pixels the paint pushes to the ink colour via `gb`. All three channels are then linear in ONE driver `drv = 16*sh + 118*lit + 34*spike` plus that ink, with the same sign, so spec luma darkens wherever the paint brightens with no internal cancellation. Measured amp_corr 0.771-0.838 over all ten variants against the 0.35 floor.

(c) OP COUNT — ~132 full-canvas-equivalents (38 in the cached field, ~60 in paint including K.finish's 18, ~34 in spec), above the 20-25 guidance but below the contract's own worked example measured in the same process. There is no Python loop over features at all, and the two np.exp calls are full-canvas, not in a loop. Measured rather than estimated: 1.15 s best for paint+spec at 2048 on a quiet machine, and 2.45x `wrap_perf_window` when the two are timed alternately in one process over 8 rounds. One trap worth recording for the next agent: this box is contended enough that absolute timings swung 1.15 s to 10 s for unchanged code — only the paired ratio is trustworthy, and the reference itself moved 0.63 s to 2.06 s between runs.
